title: Safemode evacuation and maintenance-tagging playbook for capacity-sensitive hosts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Maintenance and upgrades on Dedicated hosts currently rely on coarse drain operations that cause transient throughput cliffs for customers with reserved capacity and tight latency SLOs. We need an operational model that standardizes how we tag hosts for maintenance, enters a safemode evacuation where KV caches and warm paths are preserved where possible, and sculpts traffic progressively to avoid stepped SLO violations.

Goal: Deliver a playbook plus control-plane automation that: (1) exposes 'maintenance tags' and 'evacuation profiles' for hosts, (2) supports a safemode drain mode that coordinates KV cache warmup and selective connection handoff, (3) integrates with autoscaler policies to request hedged capacity before maintenance waves, and (4) provides runbook steps and programmatic APIs for scheduled and ad-hoc maintenance windows.
acceptance_criteria: Control plane API to assign maintenance tags to hosts and to set evacuation_profile in 1.0 (doc+schema)

A safemode drain mode implementation that: decreases incoming routing weight in 5% steps, triggers KV cache snapshot+transfer hooks when supported, and emits telemetry for per-host token throughput and SLO delta
Autoscaler will respond to a maintenance wave by provisioning hedged capacity (configurable multiplier) before drains begin in >=90% of test runs
Runbook documented with CLI commands, console steps, and rollback checklist; reviewed and approved by oncall and platform SRE

End-to-end test demonstrating a scheduled maintenance window on a dedicated pool with 3 customer reservations: measured <2% p95 latency regressions and <5% throughput loss for each reservation during maintenance window when hedging is enabled
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind dedicated-fleet feature gate. 2) Deploy control-plane changes to staging and run synthetic evictions against canary pool. 3) Enable safemode drains in a single low-risk customer pool with hedged autoscaling=1.2. 4) Monitor telemetry for 48h, iterate on weight-step timing and KV snapshot hooks. 5) Gradual ramp to all scheduled maintenance windows with training sessions for SRE and customer success. 6) Remove feature flag after 4 successful maintenance waves.
